# Progress — run `agent-harness-2026-11-07-2` (agent-harness)

What this file is: the run's journal, rendered by the harness from `entries.jsonl`, newest entry first (the 15 newest in full; every entry is in `progress-archive.md`). Each entry is one session: its feature, outcome, summary, what it tried, what it found.

The run builds the memory curator of `docs/specs/2026-11-07-memory-curator.md`, three milestones in series: **M1** a coding session's `CLAUDE.md` edit is reverted (`restrict … memory`) and facts go in the entry; **M2** an Opus `curator` session emits itemized operations (`memory-ops.json`) that the driver validates, tiers and applies on `harness-memory/<run>` behind a `memory: <run>` PR; **M3** `memlint-self` retires, `MEMORY_POLICY=pr|auto|off`, acceptance counted (`summary.memory`, the `Memory` row, `harness memory`).

How to read the feature list: `feature_list.json` is in priority order; a feature runs when it isn't passing and its `after` all pass. Each milestone's plan feature writes `docs/plans/2026-11-07-M<n>-….md`; the last feature of each milestone is its review (M1's is folded into M1-03). When every feature of a milestone passes the harness verifies it and opens its PR against `main` (`MERGE_POLICY=pr`).

How to steer: edit `INBOX.md` in this directory from the phone or `harness answer`. A line `status: stop <why>` or `status: pause` on top stops or pauses the run; answers to questions go under `## Answers`; a brief under the steering comment changes scope for the next session. Open questions are listed under the entries that asked them and in `harness needs`.

discoveries.text: The decision file holding the rejected LLM curator (for M1-03's Updated in place line) is journal/decisions/2026-10-22-context-pack.md:35 (`Rejected: an LLM curator`); the two specs (2026-10-24-memory-model.md:161, 2026-10-25-throughput-and-memory-design.md:43) are history and stay as written (default).

The eight projects for the tier fixture are agent-harness, dj-crate-streaming, hit_list, n8n-home, pathways, portfolio_site, rane-one-mixxx and voice-concierge (the projects directory the user CLAUDE.md names; read-only). rane's protected headings carry suffixes: `## Hardware facts (verified 2026-10-19 on Michael's desktop)`, `## Hardware and Mixxx rules (binding on every session)`.

Existing stub knobs M1 reuses: STUB_GOTCHA=<id> (a coding session adds a ## Gotchas line), STUB_PROJECT_FACT=<id> (its entry carries that fact affecting project), STUB_RESOLVE=<id> (later entries resolve STUB_ASK's question, not a fact: a fact-resolving knob is new). The stub's first-line role switch is `case $first in "# Retro")…` in tests/stub-claude.sh:163; a `# Curator session` branch goes beside it.

retro() in lib/driver.sh:228 is the template for curator(): restrict … nothing with retro-proposals.json rescued to $SCRATCH (not a symlink, at most 65536 bytes, changed since the start commit) and S_NOTES noted after the restrict. finish() calls retro, then SUM build/report, then record_pr, then ledger: the curator goes between the retro and record_pr, and memory.json must exist before the final SUM build for M3's summary.memory.

Tier 2 is body-only by default: the spec says tier 2 is carried to the PR for Michael and its check wants the workflow line absent from the branch, so only tier-1 ops are committed; tier 2 and 3 appear in the PR body with their `from` (M2-01 marks it *default*; see the question).
Earlier runs' coding sessions took 12–77 min (median about 30); S4's review feature took 75 min. The full suite was 640 s at init: a full-suite step gets a 1,500,000 ms timeout.

questions: Tier 2 (conventions and workflow lines): the spec says `one commit per tier` and also `carried to the PR for Michael` with the workflow line `not applied`. The list takes body-only as the default (tier-1 ops are the branch's one commit; tier 2 and 3 appear in the PR body as ready-to-paste text with provenance). If you want tier-2 ops committed as a second commit on the same branch instead, say so before M2-04 starts.
